overall.summary: The footage is materially more structured than random capture and contains enough clean units for an automated pilot. It is not yet safe for blind folder-level auto-edit because several long files contain duplicate attempts, resets, and multiple actions.

one_primary_action_per_source.finding: Short takes generally comply; four long takes contain repeated attempts or rearrangements.

pre_action_space.finding: 0068 and several long takes have generous setup space; 0070 and 0078-0080 begin after hand contact or pickup has started.

post_action_result_hold.finding: Most selected units provide 1.5-5 seconds of result hold; several failed/repeated attempts do not.

no_repeated_attempts_in_one_source.finding: 0067, 0071, 0074 and 0076 contain multiple tries or resets.

clear_action_unit_boundaries.finding: Boundaries are visually recoverable, but the long sources require semantic segmentation rather than simple start/end trimming.

auto_edit_convenience.finding: A whitelist of clean files plus extracted AU boundaries is sufficient for a controlled pilot.

per_file.issue: Five opening attempts are mixed together; one is aborted.
Recording starts with the hand already gripping the card.
Three duplicate card presentations with long dead-time resets.
Two distinct cards/actions share one file.
Number reveal and question-side flip are separated by a reset/re-presentation.
Three number-side retries precede the complete flip sequence.
Two-stage action needs an internal cut between number and question reveal.
Multiple layout builds, clears and resets; hands obscure cards; lighting hotspot shifts.
Pickup starts before recording; use a later in-point.
Pickup starts before recording; use a later in-point.
Action begins mid-pickup and result hold is shorter.
Opening is a moving camera reveal, not a static state-before.

capture_notes: All files use a consistent 9:16, 1728x3072, 59.94 fps, 10-bit HEVC profile, which is excellent for a unified vertical edit.
The white fur background gives strong product separation but introduces texture movement that can make optical motion detection noisier.
Warm localized lighting creates moving hotspots and occasional card glare; exposure/color consistency is weaker in layout shots than in box-opening shots.
Card text is generally readable when held close, but oblique angles and hand shadows reduce machine OCR confidence in several takes.
Camera framing is consistent enough for automated matching, especially 0068, 0077 and 0081.
